result.analysis_summary: The athlete performs two distinct hydration events during Recovery 2 and Recovery 4. The mechanics of drinking are consistent, but the post-hydration behavior differs: the athlete checks a watch after the first event but resumes rowing immediately after the second. Following Recovery 2, the athlete requires approximately 4-5 strokes to re-establish a steady rowing rhythm.

findings.comparison: The hydration mechanics (unscrewing, drinking, screwing) are identical in both events. However, post-hydration behavior differs: the athlete checks a watch after Recovery 2 but resumes rowing immediately after Recovery 4.
findings.counterevidence: None observed; actions are clearly visible.
findings.direct_observation: The athlete stops rowing, places the handle on the rail, picks up a water bottle, unscrews the cap, drinks, and replaces the cap.
findings.limitations: Fixed frontal camera angle; specific watch time is illegible.
findings.title: Hydration Event 1 (Recovery 2)

findings.comparison: Hydration mechanics are consistent with Event 1. Post-hydration behavior differs as the athlete resumes rowing immediately without checking a watch.
findings.direct_observation: The athlete stops rowing, drinks from a water bottle, and resumes rowing immediately after capping the bottle.
findings.title: Hydration Event 2 (Recovery 4)

findings.comparison: Transition from rest to work interval.
findings.direct_observation: The first 3-4 strokes appear slower and less fluid. By the 5th stroke, the rhythm appears steady.
